title: relay-envelope v1
description: One message through the relay (relay design 2026-10-09, section 3; relay/Envelope.ps1). The relay never reads it and cannot forge it: the body is AES-256-GCM under a fresh content key, the content key is HPKE-sealed (RFC 9180 base mode, DHKEM(P-256)/HKDF-SHA256/AES-256-GCM) to each recipient key, the canonical header is the additional data of both, and the sender signs the header, the recipients and the ciphertext - with its machine key (ES256) or, for a founder's answer, with a passkey (a WebAuthn assertion whose challenge is the SHA-256 of the same signed bytes). Version 1 IS that suite: an envelope names no algorithm to negotiate. The wire text must be exactly the canonical form relay/Envelope.ps1 writes - members in this order, no whitespace, every string from a restricted ASCII alphabet - so the signed content (header, recipients, ciphertext) has one spelling, and a parser that sees anything else refuses it. The signature is NOT part of an envelope's identity: a passkey may sign the same content more than once, and its s may come in either half, so two texts can carry one signed content; identity is the replay key from/channel/seq/nonce (Get-HordeRelayReplayKey), never a hash of the text. AES-GCM is not key-committing: a trusted sender could give two recipients different bodies, so nothing may rely on every recipient having seen the same body. SIZES ARE NOT HERE: core/Schema.ps1 has no maxLength or maxItems, so the caps (body 1 MiB, 8 recipients, the text length, clientDataJSON 1024 bytes) are enforced in relay/Envelope.ps1, as remote/Contract.ps1 does for the link.

v.description: The envelope version. A reader refuses any other, by name, before reading further.

kind.description: What the body is, within its channel (snapshot, answer, ack...). The channels name their kinds; this file only bounds the spelling.

channel.description: Which relay channel (decisions, chat...) this belongs to; with from, the stream the sequence counts.

from.description: The sender's key id: a machine's signing key, or the founder's passkey credential key.

to.description: The recipient key ids, in the order of recipients, each once, 1 to 8.

seq.description: The sender's monotonic sequence number on this channel, 0 to 2^53-1. The journal (a later pull request) refuses a repeat and reports a gap.

nonce.description: 12 random bytes as hex: the body's AES-GCM nonce, and with from, channel and seq the replay key.

ts.description: When the sender made it, in Unix milliseconds. A number, not text: PowerShell 7's ConvertFrom-Json turns date-shaped text into a DateTime (measured 2026-10-09), which would change what the parser sees.

enc.description: HPKE enc: the 65-byte ephemeral public key.

key.description: The 32-byte content key, HPKE-sealed to this recipient: 48 bytes.

ct.description: The body, AES-256-GCM: ciphertext then the 16-byte tag.

sig.description: ES256 carries value; webauthn.get carries authenticatorData, clientDataJSON and signature; session (relay/Session.ps1) carries vouchId and value, and on the first envelope of a session also vouch with its passkey assertion (authenticatorData, clientDataJSON, signature). Which members go with which alg is checked in code.

vouchId.description: session: the key id of the session key, which names the vouch it signs under.

value.description: ES256 and session: 64 bytes, r || s.

vouch.description: session: the vouch text (relay/Session.ps1), whose hash the passkey assertion beside it signs.

keyId.description: The first 16 bytes of SHA-256 of a 65-byte P-256 public point, as hex.
